explication: Apache Arrow is a multi-language data platform centered on a universal in-memory columnar format. The C++ implementation provides typed arrays, buffers, schemas, tables, compute kernels, filesystem and IPC abstractions, dataset scanning, and format adapters. Acero supplies asynchronous execution primitives for query plans, while Gandiva compiles expressions through LLVM and caches or links generated modules. Flight exposes Arrow IPC data through RPC, with authentication and a SQL-specific protocol. Parquet and ORC provide durable columnar format interoperability. C GLib, Python, R, Ruby, and MATLAB directories expose language-specific bindings; the sampled GLib and Ruby files confirm wrappers around Flight, Flight SQL, and CUDA concepts. The graph emphasizes the C++ runtime and its principal data movement and analytics paths, plus representative binding surfaces. Many subsystems are only established by the tree or README, and the provided excerpts are partial, so detailed wiring for language bindings, dataset discovery, filesystem implementations, and transport internals is intentionally omitted.
